spec: ENTERPRISE_EVAL_SPEC.md Addendum A (frozen 2026-08-08), gate = mean paired delta at k=10 over seeds {1,2,3} >= +5 F1
environment: all twelve scoreable arms cuda/bf16 — every pair is environment-homogeneous, so the within-rung gate is clean

gate_k10.read: Adaptation is NEGATIVE at the preregistered decision point: -4.5 F1, with 2 of 3 seeds clearly negative. The interval also includes zero, so this is not a measured harm either — it is a failure to demonstrate benefit.

curve_k5_NOT_THE_GATE.status: SUPERSEDED 02:15Z by the robustness check — not signal at all
curve_k5_NOT_THE_GATE.why_it_is_not_the_headline: k=5 was preregistered as a CURVE point, not the decision point. Promoting it to the headline because it came out positive is precisely the cherry-pick that retired the old +12.7 F1 claim. It may not be quoted as the wedge result, in the deck, one-pager, FAQ, paper or any investor conversation.
curve_k5_NOT_THE_GATE.what_it_legitimately_supports: CORRECTED: when written at 00:30Z this said the excluded-zero interval made k=5 real signal worth a future preregistered test. The 02:15Z sign test and jackknife refute that: 27W/20L is p=0.38 and the mean drops to +3.9 F1 without its two biggest winners. It supports no claim and does not warrant a dedicated follow-up test on its own.
curve_k5_NOT_THE_GATE.ci_excluding_zero_was_misleading_here: A parametric interval on a mean is exactly the statistic that two extreme receipts can move. This row is the worked example of why the report now requires the CI and the sign test to agree.

the_actual_finding.pattern: WEAKENED 02:15Z. At 00:30Z this was stated as 'the sign REVERSES with k: +6.9 at k=5, -4.5 at k=10' and called the finding worth more than either number. The robustness check undercuts the k=5 half: that +6.9 is two receipts, p=0.38 on win-count. So the honest version is a DIRECTIONAL difference between an outlier-driven non-result at k=5 and a broad but non-significant negative at k=10 (p=0.10).
candidate_mechanisms_untested: more in-context examples make the k-shot baseline stronger, so the adapted arm has less headroom to add
one LoRA epoch over 10 examples overfits where 5 does not
longer prompts dilute the adapted behaviour at generation time
the_actual_finding.discipline: The three candidate mechanisms below were proposed to explain a reversal that is now mostly one-sided. They remain untested and may not be stated as reasons externally; a mechanism story for an effect this fragile would be fitting noise.
the_actual_finding.what_it_is_still_worth: The k=10 side is the durable half: 29 of 60 receipts got worse and only 17 better, spread across the distribution rather than in a few blowups. That adaptation at k=10 does not help at 4B is the finding. Any claim that it HELPS at smaller k is not supported by these artifacts.

k30_arms.outcome: all six OOMed on T4 at the frozen config (max_seq 8192)
k30_arms.handling: recorded as error artifacts; no number imputed

cross_rung_caveat: The 4B rung ran GPU/bf16 while 0.5B ran CPU/fp32. Within-rung gates are clean, but any 0.5B-vs-4B SCALING statement carries a device+dtype confound and must not be made from these artifacts.
precision_context: Per experiments/ge2_power_finding_2026-08-11.json the gate is underpowered: MDE at k=10/4B is 11.3 F1 against a 5.0 F1 bar. A positive result here would have needed the same caveat; the negative result does not become a positive one because of it.
consequence_for_goal_2: The stated goal was 'one clean preregistered +5 F1 paired result at 4B'. That result does not exist: the preregistered test ran to completion and returned -4.5 F1. The product wedge still has no positive quality evidence at the decision point. This must be stated plainly to Raj and must not be softened by quoting k=5.
what_remains_live: 1.5B rung (arc-ttt-cord-scale-15b-cpu, RUNNING) — CPU/fp32, so directly comparable to 0.5B and the cleaner test of the scale claim
4B CPU bf16 rung (arc-ttt-cord-scale-4b-cpu, RUNNING) — same-rung replication that retires the device/dtype half of the cross-rung confound
0.5B gate closure — DONE 02:10Z 08-12: FAILS at -7.3 F1 (ge2_0.5b_result_2026-08-11.json)

robustness_check_added_02:15Z.why: A 95% CI is a statement about a MEAN, and a mean over 60 receipts can be carried by two of them. Added a distribution-free sign test and a drop-the-top-winners jackknife to scripts/cord_paired_power.py so every rung reports both from now on.

k5_positive_DOES_NOT_SURVIVE.read: The +6.9 F1 mean whose CI excluded zero is carried by two receipts that went from near-zero to near-perfect. Drop them and it is +3.9 F1, below the bar; drop three and it is +2.9. On a win-count basis 27 vs 20 is ordinary chance (p=0.38). The k=5 'positive' is an outlier artifact and is now barred on evidence, not just on preregistration grounds.

k10_negative_is_broad_not_outlier_driven.read: The k=10 loss shows up across the receipt distribution rather than in a few blowups - the trimmed mean matches the raw mean. It is still not significant on its own (p=0.10), so the honest reading is a failure to demonstrate benefit, not a demonstrated harm.

robustness_check_added_02:15Z.overall: At 4B, NEITHER k shows a robust effect in either direction once outliers are controlled. The gate fails and the exploratory positive evaporates.
robustness_check_added_02:15Z.new_trap_logged: 0.5b k=5 shows 34W/19L, p=0.053 - the most suggestive p in the table, and its mean is only +1.1 F1 with a CI including zero. It is 1 of 4 comparisons and the two statistics disagree, so it is NOT a result. The multiplicity and two-statistics-must-agree warnings now ship inside every power report so a future session cannot quote it as one.
